HomePage.scheduleHeading: Schedule a Visit & Get a Discount
HomePage.customersText: With Scheduled Visit Discount (SVD), you book a store visit in advance. If you arrive on time and make a purchase, you receive a pre-agreed discount. No waiting, no uncertainty, better prices.
HomePage.managersText: SVD turns planned visits into predictable demand. You know who is coming, when, and why. Discounts are offset by higher conversion, smoother operations, and better use of staff and space.

ForManagers.heroBody: Bondoutfit lets your customers book a fitting appointment at your store online — and get a discount when they show up and buy. Fewer wasted visits, more traffic on quiet days, and a simple dashboard to manage it all.
ForManagers.step1Body: They browse your collections and available slots on Bondoutfit.
ForManagers.step2Body: A visit is scheduled directly into your store's calendar — no back-and-forth.
ForManagers.step3Body: You know who is coming and when, so you can prepare and greet them properly.
ForManagers.step4Body: On arrival, they unlock a discount to use on their purchase — encouraging them to actually buy.
ForManagers.benefit1Title: More foot traffic on quiet days
ForManagers.benefit1Body: Discounts pull customers in specifically when you need them, not just at peak hours.
ForManagers.benefit2Body: Customers who book in advance are far more likely to show up and buy — no more guessing who's serious.
ForManagers.benefit3Body: Manage your schedule, discounts, and items from one place — no complicated setup.
ForManagers.benefit4Body: You decide the discount, the hours, and the items — Bondoutfit just brings the bookings.
ForManagers.demoBody: Try Bondoutfit as both a store owner and a customer, using our live demo store — no signup required.
ForManagers.finalCtaBody: Setting up your store takes a few minutes — and I'm happy to walk you through it personally.

HowItWorks.title: How the scheduled visit discount (SVD) Works
HowItWorks.step1Body: Store managers create time-specific discount offers for scheduled visits.
HowItWorks.step2Body: Customers browse available time slots and book their visit through BondOutfit.
HowItWorks.step3Body: Customer shows up at the scheduled time and checks in at the store.
HowItWorks.step4Body: Store applies the pre-announced discount to the customer's purchase.

Psychology.lede: If you've ever looked at your own discount sign and wondered why it isn't pulling its weight, you're not alone. I walked down another street today, past window after window promising twenty percent off, thirty percent off, buy-one-get-one. The signs were confident. The stores behind them were quiet.
Psychology.para2: It's a strange contradiction every retailer knows intimately: the discount is right there, printed in bold, impossible to miss — and still, most people walk straight past it. Why?
Psychology.para3: Because a discount sign asks nothing of the person looking at it. It's free to ignore. It costs nothing to walk by. And when something costs nothing, it rarely earns much attention either.
Psychology.shiftOnePara1: But something changes the moment a customer books an appointment. Suddenly there's a small promise on both sides — the customer has agreed to show up, and quietly, the discount stops being a free giveaway and turns into something they're actually going to earn.
Psychology.shiftOnePara2: That's not a coincidence. It's how people work. Ask anyone who has ever put down a deposit, confirmed their attendance at a dinner, or booked a haircut two weeks in advance — the simple act of committing changes how seriously we take what comes after. Why we crave a small commitment before a reward doesn't really matter for our purposes here. What matters is that we do.
Psychology.shiftTwoPara1: There's a second, quieter shift that happens the moment someone books a visit to your store. They stop being anonymous foot traffic and become, however briefly, expected. Someone on your team now knows they're coming. And knowing changes everything — the greeting is warmer, the attention sharper, the whole interaction less like a transaction and more like it was arranged in advance, because it was. It's also, quietly, an opportunity: for your staff, whose own charisma has more room to show when they're not just reacting to a stranger — and for the customer, who tends to let more of their own personality come through when they feel expected rather than anonymous.
Psychology.shiftTwoPara2: This is the idea behind Bondoutfit's name. Not a coupon. Not a gimmick. A bond — between your business, your staff, and the person walking through your door with an appointment already in hand.
Psychology.closing: Your discount signs aren't wrong. They're just doing half the job. Bondoutfit is the other half — the part that turns a passing glance into a kept promise.
